summary: The team is in execution mode on two fronts: launching the Intelligent China webpage this week while finalising the Knowledge website redesign, and clearing a persistent Outlook lockout that is blocking email access across devices.
summaryDetail: The most urgent item is the Intelligent China webpage launch, which is due this week and is central to the strategy of prioritising China-based programs (Asia Star and Intelligent China) for SEO and AI-search visibility. In parallel, the Knowledge website redesign is nearing a decision point: the team has settled on a two-menu structure and a BCI/BSI banner in the Knowledge section, but Joseph, Julie, and the design lead still need a 30-minute working session to mark specific feedback before Joker can implement changes. A lingering Outlook account lockout, caused by stale password caches, requires immediate team-wide action—deleting and re-logging into all email accounts on all devices and updating passwords—to restore full email functionality. Looking ahead, Joseph must draft the target areas/prompts and audience focus document and build Asia Star participant profiles to sharpen SEO/AI-search targeting, while the Google Ads conversion tracking audit awaits a brief from Joseph. The team also recently decided to put US partner programs (Stanford, Columbia) on hold for the first quarter and to opt out of the British Business Sentiment Survey, so bandwidth can stay focused on the China-based priorities.

decisions.text: Use the new password across all devices and update Outlook clients to avoid re-lockout.
Remove the standalone videos section; videos will be dispersed by topic instead.
Keep the two-menu structure with the school menu at top and knowledge menu centered.
Bring the BCI (and BSI) index banner into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage.
Use the article detail page design with prominent authors, audio, pullout quotes, and varied title font sizes as the template.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top two programs to promote, with Berkeley as an optional third priority.
Put US partner programs (Stanford, Columbia) on hold for the first quarter, revisiting later.
Include the Berkeley program in the audit phase as a test overseas program.
Opt out of the British Business Sentiment Survey 2026-2027 due to limited bandwidth
